ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Shock changes the sequence

A 56-year-old man has a hot swollen knee, fever, hypotension and confusion. Septic shock is suspected. Blood cultures can be collected promptly, but joint aspiration is temporarily delayed. Which action is most appropriate regarding antimicrobial treatment?

  1. Give a steroid injection and defer antibiotics
  2. Start empiric antibiotics promptly as part of sepsis management
  3. Wait until joint culture results are finalized
  4. Wait until the leukocyte count exceeds a fixed threshold
  5. Treat only with an intra-articular anesthetic
Answer and explanation

Start empiric antibiotics promptly as part of sepsis management

Suspected sepsis or septic shock requires immediate treatment; delayed joint sampling must not postpone antibiotics.

Option explanations

Start empiric antibiotics promptly as part of sepsis management: Suspected sepsis or septic shock requires immediate treatment; delayed joint sampling must not postpone antibiotics.

Wait until joint culture results are finalized: This would dangerously delay treatment.

Wait until the leukocyte count exceeds a fixed threshold: Sepsis treatment is not contingent on a synovial cutoff.

Treat only with an intra-articular anesthetic: This does not treat systemic infection.

Give a steroid injection and defer antibiotics: This is not appropriate treatment of suspected septic shock.
